subject: Agriculture
title: Soil Carbon Storage
description: A quick win: understand Soil Carbon Storage.

hook.text: Soil holds more carbon than all the world's plants and atmosphere combined. It's a massive carbon bank.

buildup.text: Plants pull CO2 from the air and pump carbon into the soil through their roots. Microbes lock it there.

discovery.text: Healthy soils gain carbon. Degraded soils lose it—releasing CO2 back into the atmosphere.

twist.text: Plowing releases stored soil carbon. Global cropland has lost 50–70% of its original carbon stock.

climax.text: Regenerative practices could put billions of tons of carbon back. Soil is a climate solution hiding underfoot.

punchline.text: The world's biggest carbon vault is the ground beneath your feet.

quiz.question: How much original carbon have global croplands lost?

details.summary: Soil stores more carbon than all terrestrial vegetation and the atmosphere combined—about 2,500 gigatons globally. This topic covers how carbon enters and leaves soil, why agricultural soils have lost significant carbon, and the potential for soils to help mitigate climate change.
details.whyItMatters: Agricultural soils have lost 50-70% of their original carbon due to tillage and land conversion. Rebuilding soil carbon could offset a significant portion of global emissions while simultaneously improving agricultural productivity.
takeaways: Global soils store roughly 2,500 gigatons of carbon—more than atmosphere and plants combined
Agricultural soils have lost 50-70% of their original carbon stocks through cultivation
Restoring soil carbon through better management could offset significant annual emissions

faq.question: How does carbon get stored in soil?
faq.answer: Plants capture CO2 through photosynthesis and transfer carbon to soil through root exudates, root turnover, and above-ground litter decomposition. Soil organisms process this material, and some becomes stable humus or binds to mineral particles where it can persist for decades to centuries.

faq.question: Can rebuilding soil carbon really help address climate change?
faq.answer: The French '4 per 1000' initiative calculated that increasing global soil carbon by 0.4% annually could offset all human CO2 emissions. While this is optimistic, even partial soil carbon restoration through cover crops, no-till, and compost would significantly reduce net emissions while improving.
